branch: B02/shell-listener (detached at 251d584), scoped run: capture path, "compare-sonnet"
headline: The masking net and the dedupe key hold on every ordinary shape and the Kotlin tests have teeth (12 of 12 core probes and 3 of 3 web probes went red), and run 5's findings 1-5 are fixed. One Major remains: a code separated by invisible or format characters outside the mask's list (bidi marks, U+061C, U+2062, U+034F, keycaps, tag characters) is stored readable and unmarked. The Android classes (Capture, Outbox, Heartbeat) are covered only by emulator tests I could not run.

suites.unit: 141/141 pass (pnpm test); core Kotlin 41/41 (gradle -p apps/shell/core test)
suites.e2e: my specs: 9/9 green in Playwright (FLOW-9 only logs the reload result, so its failure is recorded in results.json, not by Playwright); the branch capture.spec 9/9 on my server

findings.title: A code separated by invisible or format characters outside the mask's list is stored whole, unmarked
findings.detail: `OtpMask` joins digits across a fixed INVISIBLE set (U+200B-200F, 2060, FEFF, 00AD) and the filter strips the same set. U+202A-202E and 2066-2069 (bidi), U+061C, U+2061-2064 (invisible operators), U+034F, the keycap sequence (digit, U+FE0F, U+20E3) and tag characters (U+E0020...) are not in it, so each digit is its own 1-digit run: nothing is masked, `maybe_otp` stays 0, and the filter does not drop it either. The code is stored readable. Spec §6.2: "Digits are read as the filter reads them (any Unicode digit, across spaces, dashes, dots, brackets and invisible characters)" and D116 "no possible code is ever stored". A bank would not send these, but the rule is exactly the non-negotiable the net exists for, and run 5's Major 1 was this same family with other characters. The core suite has no test with any of these characters (QA probe 6 shows the existing zero-width test does catch shrinking the set).

findings.title: A code split across the title and text (or text and expanded text) is stored whole
findings.detail: The mask reads each field alone, so "Your OTP 482" + "913" has two 3-digit runs and nothing is masked; the filter (which does see all parts) also keeps it because a 3-digit number is not a code. Contrived, and a bank app rarely splits a code across fields; listed because §6.2 promises no code reaches storage.
findings.evidence:
EVASION split across title/text -> KEPT title=[Your OTP 482] text=[913]
AC-26 FAIL: split code kept whole across title+text: [Your OTP 482]+[913]

findings.title: The mask eats the hour of a time that follows a date
findings.detail: A date and a time written with single spaces join into one run, so "09-10-2026 21:47" becomes "••-••-•••• ••:47". The comma-space rule saves Ryt's "12/9/2026, 9:48 PM", but TNG-style "12 Oct 2026 21:47" loses its hour as well. D119 masks dates, so the date is by design; the hour and the half-masked time are collateral. Until B10 gives numbers back, a payment's stored text cannot be read for its time.
findings.evidence: VERDICT [Balance | Your balance is RM1,234.56 as of 09-10-2026 21:47.] -> keep [Your balance is RM1,234.56 as of ••-••-•••• ••:47.] maybe=false

findings.title: Whole-number amounts in other currencies are masked
findings.detail: Only RM, MYR, USD, SGD and "$" protect the number after them. "THB 2500", "EUR 1500", "IDR 150000", "¥15000", "£1500" lose their digits (and "RM 1234.5" does). A card payment abroad may print the foreign amount beside the RM one. The ringgit amount survives; spec says "the number after a currency".

findings.title: The OTP filter is quadratic in text length: 100 kB takes about 30 s on the single capture thread
findings.detail: Sentence splitting runs a regex over the growing sentence at every "no." and the ADVICE patterns rescan it. Measured on the core: 5 kB 59-137 ms, 10 kB 0.3 s, 20 kB 1.1-1.3 s, 40 kB 3.5-4 s, 100 kB 28-31 s. One executor thread serves every capture, so a huge notification stalls the rest. Android's CI log shows the platform cutting text at 1,024 characters, which would hide it on a phone; I could not run that.

HOSTILE 100k 'never ' -> keep maybe=false len=96000 in 27685ms
TIMING no.  size=40000 -> 3534ms
TIMING never  size=40000 -> 3969ms

findings.title: A payment worded "Code: 123456" is dropped (in doubt, by design)
findings.detail: "Top up RM50.00 successful. Code: 123456" is dropped as an OTP: weak keyword plus a code in the same sentence. §6.2 chooses this ("in doubt it drops") and logs it, so it shows as a gap. Recorded so the soak can watch for real top-up wordings.

findings.title: *Captured on this phone* says "as the apps wrote them" over rows whose numbers D119 now masks
findings.detail: Every kept notification has its 4+ digit runs masked, but only a row marked maybe-OTP says so. A plain row such as "on ••/•/••••, 9:48 PM" shows bullets with no explanation under a header that claims the text is as written. §6.2 asks for the line only under a marked row, so this is wording drift, not a spec breach; the owner reading samples on the soak will wonder.

findings.title: The simulator is a stand-in: fixed samples, no filter or mask, and state lost on reload
findings.detail: `sim.post()` cycles four fixed samples, `otp()` and `maybeOtp()` push fixed strings (the second already masked), and the store is zustand memory: a browser reload empties it, so "outbox survives" and "offline then sync once" cannot be walked in Chromium (sync is B07). A browser walk proves the screen, not the capture logic; the logic is proven by the Kotlin core tests and my probes. Same point as run 5 note 6.
findings.evidence: FLOW-9: rows before reload 1; after reload body mentions: 0 notifications

findings.title: The listener trusts the stored chosen list without re-running the classifier
findings.detail: `CaptureGate` only tests `packageName in chosen`; `Chosen.set` is called from `setChosen` after the classifier, but B07 will sync `capture_apps` into the same preferences. A list holding WhatsApp would be honoured by the listener. Defence in depth only; nothing writes such a list today. Not run on a device.
findings.evidence: if (p.packageName !in chosen) return Decision.Drop(DropReason.NOT_CHOSEN)   // the only check on the list

findings.title: Capture.store catches only the gate; an exception from the SQLite insert is uncaught on the capture thread
findings.detail: `outbox.insert(...)` runs outside the try/catch. A SQLiteException (disk full, corruption) in `worker.execute` reaches the thread's uncaught handler, which kills the process on Android, and the reconnect replays the same notification. Not verified on a device.
findings.evidence: outbox.insert(d.event).also { new -> if (new) Heartbeat.event(context) }   // no catch around it

findings.title: Only OTP and unreadable drops reach the drop log
findings.detail: §6.2/D115 say each drop from a chosen app is logged by time and app. `Capture.store` logs OTP and unread only; group-summary, ongoing, channel and empty drops leave no trace. A payment is never ongoing, so the soak loses little, but a mis-flagged group summary would vanish silently.
